title: Safe division
description: Create a method called dividir that receives two integers (dividend and divisor) and returns the result of the integer division. If the divisor is 0, it must throw an ArithmeticException with the message 'Cannot divide by zero'.
hints: Use an if statement to check whether divisor equals 0
To throw an exception use: throw new ArithmeticException("message")
If divisor is not 0, simply return dividendo / divisor
solutionExplanation: The method checks with an if whether the divisor is 0. If so, it throws ArithmeticException with a descriptive message. If it is not 0, it returns the result of the division. In main, try-catch is used to catch the exception when attempting to divide by zero.

title: Age parser
description: Create a method parsearEdad that receives a String and returns an int with the parsed age. If the String is not a valid number, it must throw NumberFormatException with the message 'Invalid input: ' followed by the received value. If the number is negative, throw IllegalArgumentException with the message 'Age cannot be negative'.
hints: Use Integer.parseInt(input) inside a try to convert the String to an integer
If NumberFormatException occurs, rethrow it with a custom message including the input
After parsing successfully, check whether the number is negative before returning it
solutionExplanation: The method tries to parse the String with Integer.parseInt inside a try-catch. If it fails, it rethrows NumberFormatException with a descriptive message. If parsing succeeds but the number is negative, it throws IllegalArgumentException. In main, an array of entries is iterated and both exception types are handled.
expectedOutput:
Age: 25
Error: Invalid input: abc
Error: Age cannot be negative
Age: 30

title: Data validator
description: Create a class Validar with three static methods: validarNombre(String nombre) that throws IllegalArgumentException if it is null or empty, validarEdad(int edad) that throws IndexOutOfBoundsException if the age is not between 0 and 150, and validarEmail(String email) that throws NullPointerException if it is null or ArithmeticException if it does not contain '@'. Also create a method validarTodo that calls all three and catches each exception showing the error type.
hints: For validarNombre, check whether nombre is null or nombre.isEmpty() and throw IllegalArgumentException
For validarEdad, check whether edad < 0 or edad > 150 and throw IndexOutOfBoundsException
For validarEmail, throw NullPointerException if null, and ArithmeticException if it does not contain '@'
In validarTodo, wrap each call in its own try-catch block to report all errors
solutionExplanation: Each validation method checks a specific condition and throws the corresponding exception: IllegalArgumentException for an invalid name, IndexOutOfBoundsException for an out-of-range age, NullPointerException for a null email, and ArithmeticException for an email without '@'. The validarTodo method runs each validation in its own try-catch to report all possible errors in a single call.
expectedOutput:
Name error: Name cannot be null or empty
Age error: Age must be between 0 and 150
Email error: Email must contain '@'
